# Singapore start-up Ropedia raises US$22 mil in pre-Series A round for robot-training data The robotics data company has raised US$30 million so far, and will use the latest funds to gather more training data, increase device production and expand in Singapore and the US\. Ropedia, a Singapore start-up that supplies training data for robots and physical artificial intelligence systems, has raised US$22 million \($28\.4 million\) in a pre-Series A funding round\. It did not identify the investors in the latest round, saying only that it was led by venture firms with experience in AI, deep technology and infrastructure in Southeast Asia\. The deal brings its total funding to US$30 million\. An earlier round included investors and individuals connected to Google, Andreessen Horowitz, Nvidia and Amazon, according to the company\. Ropedia's proprietary wearable devices record first-person video, depth, movement and audio as people carry out physical tasks\. The company processes that information into training material for developers seeking to teach robots how to perform tasks in real-world settings\.
